item.title: Admonition No. 26-03
item.description: In July 2024, a Texas resident (the “client”) rented a residential property in Houston, Texas. In August 2024, the client vacated the property and stopped paying rent after learning that he could not use the property as a group home.

item.title: Admonition No. 26-04
item.description: This matter came to Bar Counsel’s attention as the result of a dishonored check notice from the respondent’s IOLTA account. The respondent is a partner in a large-volume real estate closing firm that utilizes multiple IOLTA accounts.

item.title: SJC seeks amicus briefs for posted cases
item.description: The Supreme Judicial Court seeks amicus briefs on cases involving tenant protections, sports wagering, self-representation rights, and constitutional issues.

item.title: Media co. declines to produce podcasts, prompting suit
item.description: The plaintiff sued the defendant media company for declining to contract to produce podcasts for it.

item.title: Supreme Court backs parents in school gender policy case
item.description: U.S. Supreme Court sides with parents challenging California school policies on gender transitioning disclosures, citing First Amendment and due process rights.

item.title: SCOTUS sets high bar for overturning ‘persecution’ ruling
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court rules courts must defer to immigration agencies when reviewing asylum persecution determinations under the Immigration and Nationality Act.

item.title: Judge dismisses case of deported student who declined flight back
item.description: Federal judge dismisses lawsuit of Any Lucia Lopez Belloza after she declined ICE-arranged flight back to the US following deportation to Honduras.

item.title: Virginia moves to forbid schools from teaching Jan. 6 was peaceful
item.description: Virginia lawmakers passed a bill prohibiting schools from teaching that Jan. 6 was peaceful or that 2020 election fraud was widespread, marking a first for a Democratic state.

item.title: Negligence – Ransomware attack – Economic loss doctrine
item.description: Where negligence claims have been brought by a plaintiff that suffered a ransomware attack that resulted in the deletion of its stored electronic data until it paid the requested ransom, a motion to dismiss those claims should be denied because the plaintiff’s complete loss of electronic data is sufficiently tangible to qualify as property damage so as to avoid the economic loss doctrine.
